title: On-call & Incident Response Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview:

This playbook documents Redwood Inference's on-call model, incident lifecycle, runbook expectations, postmortem process, game day guidance, and customer communication templates. It is intended for all engineers, SREs, and support staff who participate in on-call rotations or incident response. The goal is to provide a predictable, repeatable process to detect, respond to, and learn from incidents while minimizing customer impact.

Scope:

- Applies to all production-facing services (hosted API, dedicated control plane, private deployments).
- Covers alerting, escalation, incident command, communications, mitigation, restoration, and retrospective.
- Does not replace service-specific runbooks; it defines standards and templates for them.

Roles & responsibilities:

1. Incident Commander (IC):
   - Owns tactical decisions, coordinates responders, and drives remediation until recovery.
   - Is typically a senior SRE or the primary on-call engineer for the affected service.
2. Primary Responder (Pager):
   - First responder who acknowledges pager and begins troubleshooting.
3. Secondary Responder:
   - Backup escalation if primary cannot resolve within defined timebox.
4. Communications Lead / Status Author:
   - Drafts and posts updates to the status page, customer comms, and internal channels.
4. Engineering Subject Matter Experts (SMEs):
   - Support deep debugging and mitigation steps for specific services.
5. Postmortem Author:
   - Drafts the retrospective and drives corrective actions after the incident.

On-call rotations and handoffs:

- Rotation model: weekly rotations for platform SREs; service-specific rotations for product teams (typically 1 week).
- Coverage: primary (24x7) and secondary coverage during the primary's off-hours.
- Handoff checklist (to be completed in Slack or rotation tool before end of shift):
  1. Confirm next on-call identity in the rotation tool.
  2. Share active incidents and their status.
  3. List any known degradations, ongoing mitigations, or planned rollbacks.
  4. Confirm access (pager, consoles, SSH, runbook links) for incoming on-call.
  5. Note any scheduled maintenance windows that could affect alerts.
- Escalation latencies: if page not acknowledged within 5 minutes, escalate to Secondary; if no response in 15 minutes, escalate to IC on-call and notify team slack channel #oncall-escalations.

Alerting & Severity classification:

- Severity levels (standardized across teams):
  - Sev 0 (P0): Complete outage or data loss impacting majority of customers; immediate IC and all-hands.
  - Sev 1 (P1): Significant functionality degraded for many customers; requires IC and cross-team coordination.
  - Sev 2 (P2): Partial degradation or isolated failures; on-call and SMEs involved.
  - Sev 3 (P3): Minor impact, work-around available; handled during business hours.
  - Sev 4 (P4): Informational/triage-only; tracked but low priority.

- Pager policy: alerts must include: service, region, brief description, time window, runbook link, and immediate mitigation steps (if any). Include links to dashboards and logs (Grafana, Loki/Elasticsearch, tracing).

Incident lifecycle (step-by-step):

1. Detect & Triage
   - Pager fires or monitoring alert. Primary responder acknowledges within 5 minutes.
   - Triage to determine severity and scope (services, regions, customers).
2. Mobilize & Assign Roles
   - IC is assigned (if not self-assigned, the escalation policy designates IC).
   - Communications lead and SMEs are added.
3. Contain & Mitigate
   - Execute runbook steps for mitigation. If no runbook, take conservative actions (traffic diversion, scaling, circuit breaker).
4. Restore
   - Restore service to acceptable SLOs or known good state.
5. Communicate
   - Post initial status message within 15 minutes of detecting a Sev0/P0 or within 30 minutes for P1.
   - Provide regular updates every 30-60 minutes for P0/P1 until resolved.
6. Close & Postmortem
   - Declare incident resolved when SLO met and stability confirmed for at least 30 minutes.
   - Postmortem must be filed within 72 hours (initial draft) and finalized within 7 calendar days.

Runbooks & playbooks (standards):

- Each production service must have a runbook that includes: owner, runbook version/date, severity mapping, quick checklist (first 10 minutes), mitigation steps, rollback procedures, key dashboards, and contact list.
- Runbook template (required sections):
  1. Title and service identifier
  2. Owner and escalation contacts
  3. Pre-conditions / triggers for this runbook
  4. Quick triage checklist (what to check first)
  5. Mitigation steps (with CLI/console commands)
  6. Rollback / failover steps
  7. Post-incident validation steps
  8. Related runbooks and links

Example runbook quick-check snippet:

# Quick triage for API 503s
# 1. Check service pods/instances
kubectl -n prod get pods -l app=api-service
# 2. Check error rate on frontend gateway
curl https://internal-grafana/api/datasources/proxy/1/api/v1/query_range?query=request_errors&...
# 3. If recent config deploy, rollback to last stable revision
ci-cd rollback --service api-service --revision <last-stable>

Pager duty & escalation policy (examples):

- Primary acknowledges within 5 minutes.
- If unacknowledged, PagerDuty escalates to Secondary after 5 minutes, and to Team Lead after 15 minutes.
- On-call rotation owner must ensure contact methods and secondary are up-to-date.

Postmortem process & template:

- Purpose: identify root cause(s), contributing factors, corrective actions, and learnings to reduce recurrence.
- Timeline:
  - T+0-72 hours: initial postmortem draft (initial facts, timeline, mitigation summary).
  - T+7 days: final postmortem with RCA and action items assigned.
- Postmortem content (required):
  1. Summary (one-paragraph impact statement)
  2. Timeline of events (with timestamps, who did what)
  3. Root cause analysis (5 whys or similar method)
  4. Contributing factors & how they bypassed defenses
  5. Corrective actions (owner, priority, due date)
  6. Preventative measures and metrics to track
  7. Lessons learned and follow-up game days or audits

- Postmortem owner must schedule a blameless review with stakeholders and track action items to completion in the team OKR or project board.

Game days & exercises:

- Purpose: validate runbooks, train on-call responders, and surface gaps in tooling or SLOs.
- Frequency: quarterly platform-wide game days and monthly service-level tabletop exercises.
- Types:
  - Full failover: simulate region outage and verify routing/fallback policies.
  - Degradation: simulate traffic spikes or slowdowns to validate autoscaling and throttling.
  - Alert fatigue: evaluate noise and tune alert thresholds.
- Game day postmortem: short-form report with objectives, outcomes, and action items.

Status page & customer communications templates:

- Use Statuspage for public incidents and internal status channel for customer-sensitive issues. Communications lead is responsible for posting and updating.
- Customer comms templates (examples):

Initial acknowledgement (public/status page):

Title: Investigating: Elevated error rates for Redwood API
Impact: A subset of requests to the Redwood API may see 5xx errors or timeouts. Customers may experience increased latency or failures.
Affected Services: Redwood API (us-west-2)
Started: 2026-02-10T09:12:00Z
Next update: within 30 minutes

Update (example):

Title: Update: Elevated error rates for Redwood API - mitigation in progress
Impact: Error rates have improved from 12% to 4% after rolling back the recent proxy config. The team continues to monitor; customers may see intermittent failures.
Actions: Rolled back proxy config; scaling increased by +20% in us-west-2.
Next update: within 60 minutes or sooner if status changes.

Resolution (example):

Title: Resolved: Elevated error rates for Redwood API
Impact: Service restored to normal operation. We will publish a postmortem within 7 days.
What happened: A proxy configuration pushed earlier caused downstream connection resets, leading to increased 5xx responses.
Customer impact: Some customers experienced increased error rates for ~45 minutes.
Follow-up: Postmortem scheduled; corrective actions include gated deploys and pre-deploy canary checks.

Templates for direct customer email (for high-impact incidents):

Subject: Incident resolved - Redwood API degraded in us-west-2 (ID: RWI-2026-02-10-01)
Body:
Hello [Customer Name],

We experienced elevated error rates for the Redwood API in us-west-2 between 09:12-09:57 UTC on 2026-02-10. Some requests returned 5xx errors or timed out. We have restored full service and are performing a post-incident review. We will notify you when the postmortem is available.

If you experienced data loss or other customer-impacting issues, please contact support@redwood.ai and include incident ID RWI-2026-02-10-01.

Regards,
Redwood Inference Support

Tools & integrations:

- Alerting: PagerDuty (primary), Opsgenie for partner escalations.
- Monitoring: Grafana (dashboards), Prometheus (metrics), Loki/Elasticsearch (logs), Jaeger (traces).
- Communications: Slack (#oncall, #oncall-escalations), Statuspage (public), Zendesk/Intercom for customer tickets.
- Runbook storage: Confluence service pages linked from runbook index.

SLOs, error budgets & metrics to track:

- Platform API availability SLO: 99.9% monthly (target).
- Latency SLOs: p95 request latency < 200ms for small responses.
- Error budget burn rate monitoring: alert if 7-day burn rate > 2x baseline.
- Key incident metrics to capture: mean time to acknowledge (MTTA), mean time to mitigate (MTTM), mean time to recover (MTTR), number of customer-facing incidents by severity.

After-action & continuous improvement:

- Every postmortem must list owners for corrective actions and target dates. Incidents that result in Sev0/P0 require a follow-up audit and a verified remediation before the next release window.
- Track recurring incident causes quarterly and prioritize engineering work in the roadmap.

Appendices:

A. Contact matrix (short sample):
- Platform SRE Pager: +1-555-0101 (PagerDuty)
- On-call Slack: @oncall
- Incident commander escalation: eng-leads@redwood.ai

B. Runbook checklist (10-minute):
1. Acknowledge page and post in #oncall (service, severity, short summary).
2. Check key dashboards (error rate, latency, downstream errors).
3. Identify recent deploys or config changes.
4. If user-facing, post initial status page notice.
5. If no runbook or unclear, escalate to IC and follow conservative mitigation.

C. Communication templates (copyable) for initial, update, and resolution (see examples above).

D. Postmortem template link: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/postmortem-template

E. Runbook template link: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/runbook-template
